crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Citation Graphs Over Time
children.blurb: Citation graphs over time are the study of how scholarly references accumulate, connect and shift across years, rather than as a single frozen snapshot.

children.name: Clustering Papers by Meaning
children.blurb: Clustering papers by meaning groups research works according to what they are about rather than where they were published or who wrote them.

children.name: How a Paper Is Cited
children.blurb: How a paper is cited covers the paths a reference takes from one work to the next: who cites whom, in what context, and how those links accumulate into a citation graph.

children.name: Bridge Studies Between Fields
children.blurb: Bridge studies between fields are research works that connect two or more disciplines by tracing how methods, findings or vocabulary move from one to the other.

children.name: Forecasting Research Trends
children.blurb: Forecasting research trends is the practice of using citation networks, publication records and text signals to estimate which topics, methods or authors are likely to grow or fade in the near term.

sections.body: Citation mapping and discovery is the work of treating the scholarly record as a structure rather than a pile, so that a reader can see which papers lean on which, which ones cluster by meaning, and where a line of work is heading. In practice, artificial intelligence is used to parse reference lists at scale, resolve messy author and venue names, embed abstracts and full texts into vectors, and lay out graphs that would be unreadable if drawn by hand. Systems built on this work surface related papers, flag likely missing citations, and group thousands of documents into neighborhoods that share vocabulary and method. The output is not a verdict on quality, it is a navigational aid, and the underlying judgments about relevance still come from people reading the work.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The mechanical parts are largely settled. Reference parsing, entity resolution, and similarity search over embeddings work well enough to be relied on for discovery, and graph layouts scale to very large corpora. What remains hard is meaning. Citation counts conflate influence with fashion, negative citations look identical to supportive ones unless someone reads the sentence, and clustering by embedding tends to merge fields that share vocabulary but not methods. Trend forecasting is the weakest area, because research directions bend with funding, tooling, and fashion in ways no model of past citations captures, and confident extrapolations from citation curves have a poor record. The honest limit is that these tools narrow the search space, they do not tell you what matters.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here move from structure to interpretation. Citation Graphs Over Time is the foundation, showing how links accumulate and decay and why a graph drawn this year looks different from one drawn a decade ago. Clustering Papers by Meaning takes the same corpus and groups it by content rather than connection, which is what you read when you want to find a field you cannot yet name. How a Paper Is Cited is the close reading page, about the difference between a passing mention and a load-bearing one, and it is the corrective to any purely numerical view. Bridge Studies Between Fields sits where clusters overlap, covering the papers that connect two literatures and the people who can read both. Forecasting Research Trends is the speculative end, and it is best read last, after the earlier pages have shown how much of the signal is noise.
